steps.sub: accurate if it actually reaches the customer

steps.label: INVENTORY COUNT

steps.label: PRICE
steps.sub: accurate if it matches what's really charged

code:
SELECT
    c.CustomerId,
    c.Email AS CurrentEmail,
    r.Email AS ReferenceEmail
FROM dbo.Customers AS c
JOIN dbo.CustomerReference AS r
    ON c.CustomerId = r.CustomerId
WHERE c.Email <> r.Email;
caption: Rows where the current value disagrees with a source you trust more.

steps.label: SYSTEM OF RECORD
steps.sub: the source app where the value originates

steps.label: EXTERNAL VERIFICATION
steps.sub: a postal, banking, or ID-format service

steps.label: MANUAL CONFIRMATION
steps.sub: a physical count or audited sample

steps.label: REFERENCE TABLE
steps.sub: a dataset your org already trusts

code:
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS TotalCompared,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.AuditedValue <> t.CurrentValue
             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Mismatches
FROM dbo.AuditSample AS s
JOIN dbo.TargetTable AS t
    ON s.RecordId = t.RecordId;
caption: No full reference table needed — an audited sample still yields a trackable accuracy rate.
